prompt: A heart monitor trace is modelled by $y = 3\sin(6x)$, where $x$ is in degrees. How many degrees wide is ONE full beat?
hint: One full beat is one full wave — that is the PERIOD.

hints.text: One full beat is one full wave — that is the PERIOD.

explanation: On a monitor, the trace repeats the same bump over and over. One repeat is one period.
The number in front of $x$ inside the sine is $6$, so the wave is squeezed six times tighter.
Period $= 360 \div 6 = 60^\circ$. The amplitude $3$ tells you how TALL the bump is, not how wide.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the beats in one turn
steps: b = 6 means 6 whole waves fit into 360°.

alternativeExplanations.title: Follow the inside
steps: A wave finishes when the inside of the sine has run from 0 all the way to 360.
The inside is 6x, so 6x = 360 gives x = 60. One beat spans 60° of x.
